Miller & Lux, a 7,000 sq ft, two-floor steakhouse from chef Tyler Florence (designed by Ken Fulk), opened Sept 28, 2021 at 7 Warriors Way Ste 208 in Thrive City -- named after Henry Miller and Charles Lux, meatpacking-district butchers who once occupied the arena's site.

Cupcakin' Bake Shop opened at 7 Warriors Way Unit 200 in Thrive City on Oct 18, 2022, its fifth Bay Area location (after two in Berkeley, one in Oakland, one in Walnut Creek), adjacent to the Warriors Team Shop.
Siren Cafe & Bar, a seafood-focused cafe and bar from Michael Iglesias and Joseph Cleveland of Dos Ojos Hospitality, opened as a pop-up at Thrive City around February 2025.

The Sarap Shop, a Filipino-American food business from Kristen Brillantes, JP Reyes and James Brillantes (previously a food truck, with a flagship in SOMA Pilipinas), operates a stand at 1 Warriors Way in Thrive City; no specific opening date found.

The owner identified that DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (formerly tracked as status.csv blklot 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (formerly blklot 8722063) byte-identical geometry -- one shared master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). This made the two records' polygons fully overlapping on the map -- a click anywhere in the shared area could resolve to either record, and each record's own "Where it is" mini-map showed the wrong footprint. Migrated both records off status.csv onto hand-derived, non-overlapping real geometry: Chase Center (record_id mission_bay_chase_center) is now the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints subtracted out; Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (record_id mission_bay_uber_3_4) is now the union of those same two real OSM footprints. The owner also identified that Harmonic Brewing's own standalone taproom building, at the NE edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206, confirmed via its own DataSF business-registration address and geocoded location), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208, confirmed inside the arena's own footprint) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures -- Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new geometry (it falls within the parcel-minus-Uber-towers remainder) rather than tracked as a separate record. Re-running the retail spatial join (src/join_retail.py) against the corrected geometry surfaced three more real, previously-untracked Thrive City tenants -- Cupcakin' Bake Shop, Siren Cafe & Bar and The Sarap Shop -- added separately; see those changelog rows.

The owner asked whether the P12/P13/P15 sources (the interim parcels hosting Spark Social SF, Stagecoach Greens and Urban Sprouts) included SF Rec & Park's own community-workshop decks. They didn't yet; added all three, each verified by fetching the PDF directly. Community Meeting #3 (Apr 29, 2025, 83 pages) has individually labeled concept-plan pages for P12, P13 and P15 -- food trucks, outdoor dining and a pavilion on P15, matching Spark Social SF's current use; soccer pitches and outdoor fitness on P12 -- plus an alternative option for P12. Design-workshop concepts, not an adopted final plan: the design team was only selected via an Aug 2025 OCII/MBDG RFQ, after Workshop 3.

Francois Boulevard's own geometry (mission_bay_500_terry_francois.geojson) -- it had only ever captured 1 of 3 real DataSF footprint pieces sharing its mblr (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the real ~8636 sq m building), now corrected to the union of all 3; added 1401 Third Street (~222,000 sq ft office building, built 2009, tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, 469,726 sq ft structure, built 2009) as new real records. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them -- left undocumented rather than guessed, same treatment as the already-investigated 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This audit method (real polygonized blocks + building-footprint coverage fraction) is more rigorous than the ad hoc satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the prior two passes and should be the standard going forward for any future Mission Bay completeness claim.

Mission Bay 7E/7W spot-check (prompted by the owner asking directly about that block): matched the plan's block '7E'/'7W' label position against real street geometry (both letters resolve to the same coarse real block, since no mapped street divides them) and found a real, previously untracked building on its own standalone Assessor lot (blklot 8711227, recorded 2012) -- the Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House, 540 Mission Bay Blvd North: a 5-story, 80-room nonprofit free lodging house for families of children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, built 2016. Identified via the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Roll API (property_location, use code, year built, welfare exemption all cross-checked) after OpenStreetMap/Overpass lookups failed to name it -- added only once that gave a citable address and name, not from proximity alone. A second candidate found the same way, at 1600 Owens St (blklot 8709020) near block 18A/18B, turned out to be a false lead: the DataSF Assessor tax-roll lookup that identified it as 'Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices' also revealed it was already tracked as a real parcel-joined status.csv row (added in an earlier pass with more detailed sourcing than this one found) -- check_geometry_quality.py --strict caught the 3,023 sq m overlap before it was committed, and the duplicate file was removed rather than left in. This is a reminder that the real-block coverage-fraction audit method (comparing DataSF building footprints against tracked geometry) can itself under-report coverage when a real building's Assessor parcel boundary and its DataSF building-footprint outline don't line up exactly -- it found a genuine gap here, but also one false positive, and both needed the same tax-roll cross-check to resolve either way.

Mission Bay Block 6E real-parcel find, prompted by the owner directly asking why the map only showed 7E and not 7W. Investigating that pushed a re-check of the plan-to-real-world transform's local accuracy: the label positions for 7E and 7W (fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core) drift enough this far out that the 7W label position actually lands inside a different, adjacent block's building -- 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit, mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats, groundbreaking reported September 2016) that was genuinely untracked. Confirmed via its own standalone Assessor parcel (blklot 8711505) and DataSF's Historical Secured Property Tax Roll; DataSF's Building Footprints layer only captures small roof-edge fragments of this building (confirmed against satellite imagery), so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly rather than the incomplete footprint layer. Added as a real status.csv row, not an approximate trace. This is a concrete instance of the known limitation already logged for the PDF-transform approach: label positions this far from the control-point cluster cannot be trusted for identifying which real building a plan label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax-roll API) -- exactly the caveat under which the transform was adopted in the first place.

Mission Bay Block 7W: the owner correctly pushed back that 7W sits east of 4th St per the drawing (not west, where the block-6E find landed) -- confirmed against the plan's own drawing (a crop showing Block 6 and Block 7 as adjacent, split by 4th St, with 6/7's own W/E split being relative to Merrimac St vs 4th St, not to which side of 4th St the whole block sits on). Re-searched the corrected area (east of 4th St, between it and the already-tracked Family House/7E) and found Five88 (588 Mission Bay Blvd North, blklot 8711226): 200 affordable apartments (198 affordable plus a manager's unit), developed by Related California with Chinatown Community Development Center, architect David Baker + Partners, groundbreaking April 2015, occupancy targeted September 2016. SocketSite's own January 2015 coverage explicitly names it 'Block 7 West,' confirming the match. As with Block 6E, DataSF's Building Footprints layer records no footprint of its own for this parcel, so the real Assessor parcel boundary is used directly. Fixed a resulting 117 sq m real-vs-real overlap at the shared property line with Family House (7E) by trimming Family House's DataSF footprint, the same pattern used for prior real-parcel-vs-real-footprint overlaps this project.

Mission Bay tracker batch: verified blocks 4W, 5, P6 and 6W per the street-anchored method (docs/briefs/mission_bay_block_inventory.csv). 4W = Strata at Mission Bay (555 Mission Rock St, already tracked, anchored to Mission Rock St next to the confirmed 4E parcel). 5 = Azure Apartments (690 Long Bridge St, already tracked, address matches Long Bridge St exactly). P6 = Mission Bay Kids' Park (already tracked, adjacent to block 5). 6W = Sister Lillian Murphy Community (671-691 China Basin St, already tracked) -- while re-verifying this one against the real street layer, found and fixed an isolated wrong site tag ('Mission Bay North' when it should read 'Mission Bay South', confirmed via a point-in-polygon check against the official redevelopment-area boundary); its two immediate neighbors added in the same original pass (MB360, MB360 1200 4th St) were correctly tagged, so this was an isolated slip, not systemic.

Mission Bay South Blocks 15A, 15B, 16A, 16B: the owner correctly pushed back on treating 'confirmed vacant' as a stopping point -- per this project's own Mission Rock precedent, an unbuilt block gets the same transform-and-register discipline as a built one, not just a note that it's empty. Traced all four using real street geometry (src/block_fit.py load_blocks()) rather than the fragile PDF transform, then trimmed against src/street_geometry.py's fuller street buffer, which caught something block_fit.py's own street source had missed: Mission Bay Boulevard South actually cuts across the block's north edge. 16B was also trimmed against the already-tracked Mission Bay Preliminary Utilities Plant at its east edge. All four use status 'planned' and the plan's own light-blue UCSF/institutional land-use color -- no specific named project was found for this parcel, so the record says so rather than guessing one. Currently an operating surface parking lot, satellite- and building-footprint-confirmed.

Mission Bay South Blocks 18A, 18B, 22: continuing the same correction as Blocks 15A/15B/16A/16B -- traced from real street geometry (src/block_fit.py) and trimmed against the fuller street buffer (src/street_geometry.py), registered as status 'planned' rather than left as an unmapped gap. 18A/18B use the plan's own light-blue UCSF/institutional color (currently an operating surface parking lot west of the Owens St curve, satellite-confirmed). Block 22 is drawn in the plan's own distinct park-green, so it's registered as a future open space (a landscaped lawn with trees today, not yet a formally named park in any source found) rather than folded into the UCSF institutional blocks around it.

Mission Bay South Block 22 (park): status corrected from 'planned' to 'complete'. This block had been traced from real street geometry and registered as a future park based on satellite imagery (a landscaped lawn with trees, no dirt, no structure) -- evidence consistent with either a finished small park or an interim-landscaped future site. The owner has been on site and confirmed it is complete. That ambiguity should have been flagged as a question rather than resolved by assumption; noted for future passes. A follow-up DataSF Assessor/Building-Footprints check found no structure on the site and traced the dominant underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder plus edge fragments of the scattered UCSF campus parcel already flagged for block 17AB -- consistent with open land, but it was the owner's on-site visit, not this lookup, that settled 'complete' vs 'planned'.

Mission Creek Park South Extension Project (P2 and P8): added two new approximate-boundary records after the owner identified this as a real, funded project (told construction breaks ground Q4 2026) while reviewing zoomed map+drawing pairs for the Mission Bay tracker. Confirmed via SF Recreation & Parks' own project page and its schematic-design PDF (Feb 2022 CAC materials): the project explicitly covers OCII plan parcels P2 and P8 by name, extending Mission Creek Park west under I-280 along Mission Bay Drive/Channel Street to the Mission Bay Circle roundabout -- 5.7 acres of new open space (expanded community garden, meadow, berms, bike path) plus a new Stormwater Pump Station No. 4 and service yard at P8. Construction reported starting late 2026/early 2027, matching what the owner was told. Traced approximate boundaries against the currently-visible graded/disturbed extent (not a surveyed footprint), trimmed against real street geometry per this project's standing rule for newly-traced blocks, and clearly caveated as pending final construction. Supersedes P8's earlier treatment as plain non-developable freeway-frontage land.

Block 20 / 17AB / 17C reattribution: Smith Cardiovascular Research Building and Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building had been grouped under Mission Bay's plan block 20 (described as 'between Nelson Rising Lane and Gene Friend Way'), but a real street-centerline check shows both actually sit north of Nelson Rising Lane, matching plan blocks 17AB and 17C instead -- the owner named the same two buildings by their clinical/informal names ('UCSF Cardiovascular Care and Prevention Center' and 'Helen Diller Cancer Research Office') while reviewing the 17AB/17C zoomed map+drawing pair, which is what prompted the recheck. Mission Bay tracker batch: dropped label 'A' from the 118-label inventory per the owner's direct instruction (117 labels going forward -- see docs/briefs/mission_bay_review_items.md for the reasoning this session found, which didn't independently support 'A' as spurious but deferred to the owner's call). Status 'existing' (pre-existing infrastructure untouched by redevelopment). Adding its real parcel boundary surfaced a 7212 sqm overlap with Mission Creek Park's existing OSM boundary, which had always overreached into the pump station's fenced site -- trimmed Mission Creek Park's geometry to remove the overreach rather than the new, more specific parcel.

Mission Bay NP1-NP5 resolved: reviewed each with the owner via zoomed map+drawing pairs, one at a time. All five are segments of one continuous shoreline path/landscaping strip along Mission Creek's north/west bank (from 235 Berry St down past Edgewater, under the I-280 overpass, to the Channel Pump Station) -- already covered end to end by the existing real, OSM-sourced Mission Creek Park polygon.
